title: Summarization
explain: For a model that compresses an article, meeting or ticket into a short, faithful, useful text, there is no single correct string, so scoring mixes reference checks, rubrics and judges. The key checks are faithfulness (every claim supported by the source), key-point recall, attribution and temporal accuracy, and privacy, each with its own gate. ROUGE is only a cheap regression signal. (忠实度第一, 覆盖度第二.)
model:
| Dimension | How | Gate |
|---|---|---|
| Faithfulness | judge: claim-level entailment against source | no key hallucination (P0) |
| Key-point recall | reference: expert checklist | no missed decisions (P0) |
| Attribution | claim-level: who owns / said what | no swapped owners (P0) |
| Temporal accuracy | claim-level | done vs planned not confused (P0) |
| Privacy | rules + judge | zero severe leaks (P0) |
| Salience | pairwise or checklist | core beats trivia |
| Conciseness, structure | ratio, format checks | target compression, hard formats |
| Audience fit | judge | meets level (P2) |

**Judges:** claim-level entailment (split into atomic claims, label supported / contradicted / not mentioned), key-point checklist, pairwise preference (randomize order), humans to audit the judge.

**Slices:** short to very long and multi-document; meetings, design docs, tickets, research; duplicated or conflicting facts; action items explicit, implicit, absent; PII or confidential content.

**Gate:** faithfulness, key-point coverage and privacy each separately, reported by length and type. Compare [RAG QA](#/sd/f/eval-rag-qa).

details.a: Split the summary into atomic claims, give a judge (or NLI model) each claim with the source, and classify it supported, contradicted or not mentioned. 10 supported of 12 claims is 0.83; both the contradicted and the unsupported claim are hallucinations. A single holistic rating misses one bad claim in twelve.

details.q: What is key-point recall and how is it paired with compression?
details.a: The share of expert-listed key decisions the summary contains: 5 of 8 is 0.625. Report it with compression: a 4,000-token transcript summarized in 200 tokens is 5% (20x), which is only good if recall of the key points holds.

details.q: Why is ROUGE a poor primary metric?
details.a: It counts word overlap. 'The board did not approve the budget' versus 'The board approved the budget' overlap almost completely though the meaning flipped, and good paraphrases score low. Use it as a cheap regression signal; gate on entailment and key points.

details.q: What failure does an attribution check catch?
details.a: Wrong associations with all words present: the source says Alice will migrate the database by Friday; the summary says Bob will. Treat owner, deadline and status as explicit checklist fields at the claim level.

details.q: Average faithfulness is 0.96 but customers say long documents lose the conclusion. What is the evaluation fix?
details.a: Slice by input length and document type, and add long-document key-point recall where the key points sit late or in the middle of the input. Averages hide slice failures and long inputs expose positional bias.

details.q: How do you use pairwise preference judges safely?
details.a: They are good for choosing between candidate summaries on overall faithfulness, coverage and brevity. Randomize the order to counter position bias, control for length bias, and compare the judge against human labels before relying on it.

details.q: How would you handle sensitive data in summaries?
details.a: Add a privacy dimension: rules and detectors for PII and confidential markers in the output, plus slices of inputs that contain such content. Treat any severe leak as a separate zero-tolerance gate, not part of an average.
